text:
maria_sales: Quick ask from prospect 'MedLedger' — POC scope: EU-only tenant, BYOK mandatory, strict region-bind to ireland for keys, frankfurt allowed only for compute failover but keys must remain in ireland. They also want the subprocessors CSV and a rough cost delta for a pinned tenant. Is this possible? cc @kai_infra @nina_security

kai_infra: Short: Dedicated or Private works. Hosted can't enforce key-region binding reliably. Important callout: if keys are bound to eu-west-1 and failover routes to eu-central-1, operations must either replicate keys or allow gateway-level wrapping. Replication requires customer-side key replication or explicit consent in addendum.

nina_security: Subprocessors CSV I can provide. Common EU subprocessors: AWS (eu-west-1, eu-central-1), GCP (europe-west3), Azure (northeurope) — include Azure if customer requires provider-level inventory, Cloudflare (CDN), Fastly (edge cache), Datadog (metrics), Sentry (errors), HashiCorp Vault (KMS partner). I'll drop the signed CSV to the ticket.

maria_sales: Please give one sentence about KMS for their questionnaire: who holds key material and whether HSM attestation exists.

nina_security: "Customer-managed keys supported on Dedicated/Private with HSM-backed BYOK; keys can be region-scoped on request. Hosted uses Redwood-managed keys by default; Hosted BYOK is available only under a legal addendum and with extra attestation."

kai_infra: Note on failover behavior: we can do compute failover to frankfurt but if key_policy.region_restrict == true then requests will be blocked unless keys are replicated. We can also configure a soft-failover (return error to client) vs hard-failover (route to frankfurt and attempt to use replicated keys). Need customer to choose.

kai_infra: Minimal routing + kms example (for infra team):

```json
{ "tenant": "medledger-poc", "routing": { "mode": "pin", "primary": "eu-west-1", "failover": ["eu-central-1"], "failover_mode": "blocked_if_key_unavailable" }, "kms": { "mode": "byok_hsm", "region_bind": "eu-west-1", "replication": "customer_option" } }
```

maria_sales: They want p95 latency target: 60ms token p95. Any sizing note?

kai_infra: For 60ms p95 we need low-concurrency GPU shapes and a reserved pool. If they expect moderate traffic (20 rps, avg seq 100 tokens) plan for 1 reserved GPU cluster + spare capacity. Pinning/reservation uplifts typically: reservation fee (~$4k-$8k/mo) + token price uplift (~15-30%) depending on model and exact instance types. Exact quote needs rps and seq len.

nina_security: KMS replication caveat to add to questionnaire: "If keys are region-bound, cross-region failover requires either customer-managed key replication or a contractual exception allowing secure key wrapping in the failover region. BYOK import/attestation timeline 3-7 business days post-PO."

ops_bot: Ticket created: POC-2098. Uploaded: EU-attestation-pack, subprocessors_signed.csv, and preliminary pricing band. Ops notes: Dedicated tenant provisioning 5-8 business days after PO + capacity confirmation. BYOK HSM import + attestation 3-7 business days.

maria_sales: Can someone paste a tiny latency-check script I can give their infra team to run from their Ireland office?

kai_infra: Small curl loop (bash):

```bash
# run from customer office in Ireland
for i in {1..150}; do
  t0=$(date +%s%3N)
  curl -s -X POST https://eu.api.redwood.example/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"test_ping"}' >/dev/null
  t1=$(date +%s%3N)
  echo $((t1-t0))
done | sort -n | awk 'END{print "p95:"$(int(NR*0.95))}'
```

nina_security: I'll attach the subprocessors CSV and the one-line KMS sentence to the questionnaire draft in the ticket. Maria, ask them whether they can replicate keys or accept a failover exception; their answer drives legal language.

maria_sales: Will do. Thanks team :white_check_mark:
